headline: Tk 16.25 crore gold: 80 gold bars recovered from airport workers’ shoes
summary: Customs officials seized 9.34kg of gold from two airline staff members arriving from Dubai at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: Customs intelligence officials recovered 80 gold bars weighing approximately 9.34kg from the shoes of two airline staff members at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.
The two staff members were intercepted by the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID) after acting on a tip-off, as they arrived on an Emirates Airlines flight from Dubai.
Each gold bar weighed around 117 grammes, with the total market value of the seized gold estimated at approximately Tk 16.25 crore.
The gold bars were allegedly concealed inside the shoes using a special method to evade customs checks.
The CIID is currently investigating the origin of the gold, the intended recipient, and all other individuals involved in the smuggling attempt.

The gold bars were allegedly concealed inside the shoes using a special method to evade customs checks.

headline_marked: Jamaat leader [[Akhtaruzzaman denied bail, sent to jail]] over airport incident
headline: Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman denied bail, sent to jail over airport incident
summary: A Dhaka court has ordered the incarceration of retired Major Akhtaruzzaman following allegations of misconduct at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate's court has denied bail to Jamaat-e-Islami leader and retired Major Akhtaruzzaman, ordering him to be sent to jail.
The charges include creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, obstructing government duties, and physically assaulting a security officer.
Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by DB police on Friday evening from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area.
The incident occurred last Thursday morning when a 34-member Jamaat delegation arrived from Medina. Due to high passenger volume, long lines formed for trolleys.
It is alleged that some protocol assistants broke the line rules to collect trolleys, leading to tensions over luggage delays and the lack of available Zamzam water.
Following the bail denial, Jamaat activists gathered at the court premises and chanted slogans, leading to arguments and scuffles between activists and BNP-leaning lawyers.
The court had previously granted a one-day remand for Akhtaruzzaman after the investigation officer requested five days of custody.
caption:
Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman sent to jail after bail is denied in a case involving airport misconduct.

A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate's court has denied bail to Jamaat-e-Islami leader and retired Major Akhtaruzzaman, ordering him to be sent to jail.

The charges include creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, obstructing government duties, and physically assaulting a security officer.

Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by DB police on Friday evening from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area.

The incident occurred last Thursday morning when a 34-member Jamaat delegation arrived from Medina. Due to high passenger volume, long lines formed for trolleys.

It is alleged that some protocol assistants broke the line rules to collect trolleys, leading to tensions over luggage delays and the lack of available Zamzam water.

Following the bail denial, Jamaat activists gathered at the court premises and chanted slogans, leading to arguments and scuffles between activists and BNP-leaning lawyers.

The court had previously granted a one-day remand for Akhtaruzzaman after the investigation officer requested five days of custody.
